title: Authentication vs Authorization

searches.query: "Authentication vs Authorization" interview production tenant object access
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: OWASP: Authentication Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Identity proof, reauthentication, safe responses and protection of authentication endpoints; deployment-specific choices remain explicit.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

sources.title: OWASP: REST Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: API credentials, token/access controls, safe error/log handling and TLS; API keys alone are insufficient for every sensitive resource.

sources.title: IETF RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
sources.supportRationale: Algorithm verification, trusted keys, issuer/audience and distinct JWT usage profiles; not a universal authorization or revocation protocol.

sources.title: OWASP: Session Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Opaque session lifecycle, cookie scope, regeneration, expiry and server-side invalidation; flags do not replace authorization/CSRF controls.

scenarios.theme: A valid customer fetches another tenant’s invoice. Where is the fix?
scenarios.assumptions: The token is genuine but the endpoint accepts any invoice ID. Tenant separation is required. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Authentication vs Authorization to other invoice.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A valid customer fetches another tenant’s invoice. Where is the fix?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Resolve and authorize the object/action within trusted tenant scope at the billing owner, test list/download/batch paths and reject untrusted tenant assert

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Scoped queries and policy checks add work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Random IDs reduce guessing but cannot replace authorization; a legitimate cross-tenant administrator needs an explicit scoped policy.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: The gateway denies a request but the internal service accepts it. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: A direct backend route trusts caller-supplied identity headers. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Authentication vs Authorization to direct backend.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The gateway denies a request but the internal service accepts it. What changes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Establish authenticated/protected propagation, discard spoofable headers and enforce the domain action/resource policy on all backend paths.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Repeated checks and context propagation cost effort

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A network boundary can reduce exposure but cannot prove every internal caller has the requested tenant permission.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz, rest; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A removed role still permits refunds. What is the revocation contract?
scenarios.assumptions: Cached claims outlive the promised immediate permission change. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Authentication vs Authorization to role removal.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A removed role still permits refunds. What is the revocation contract?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: For the sensitive refund, consult authoritative current policy or enforce a supported policy/version invalidation boundary, then align token/cache lifetime

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Fresh checks add latency and outage coupling

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Bounded stale access may fit low-risk views, but must not be advertised as immediate revocation.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz, jwt; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: The policy service times out. Should every authenticated request pass?
scenarios.assumptions: This action accesses private invoices and requires a current permission decision. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Authentication vs Authorization to policy outage.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The policy service times out. Should every authenticated request pass?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Deny or return a controlled unavailable outcome without performing the protected action; recover the dependency and expose safe diagnostics.

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A deliberately bounded cached-policy fallback can suit another documented risk model, but a timeout cannot manufacture permission.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A user loses access while their export waits in a queue. Can it run?
scenarios.assumptions: The export contains private data and execution occurs hours after submission. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Authentication vs Authorization to queued action.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A user loses access while their export waits in a queue. Can it run?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Define execution-time authorization and delegated scope, recheck required current access before producing/releasing private output and give revoked work a

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Rechecks add policy dependencies and can cancel previously accepted work

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Submission-only authorization is a different explicit contract with a longer exposure window.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authz, authn; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: A stolen active session changes recovery credentials. Was login enough?
scenarios.assumptions: The operation is high-impact and the product supports recent stronger authentication. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Authentication vs Authorization to sensitive change.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A stolen active session changes recovery credentials. Was login enough?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Require the action’s configured recent reauthentication/stronger assurance, authorize the account change and rotate/revoke affected session state under a r

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Additional friction can interrupt users

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Stronger authentication does not replace object/action authorization or make an already compromised browser harmless.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to authn, session; interview frequency is not claimed.

publicDisclosure: Researched 2026-11-17. These are adapted production scenarios informed by concept-specific interview searches and the named references below. The System Design Primer provides core orientation where applicable; technical guarantees use the mapped primary sources. Exact interview frequency, rankings and company attribution were not independently verified. Security protocol and runtime examples state their assumptions; the questions test reasoning rather than a universal product recommendation.
